title: Cædmon's Hymn
author: Cædmon (as preserved by Bede)
source_notes: West Saxon version preserved in the Old English Bede, MS Cambridge Kk.3.18 and others. Translation by Albert S. Cook, 1898.
reading_notes: The earliest datable Old English poem. According to Bede, Cædmon was an illiterate lay brother at Whitby who received the gift of poetry in a dream. Nine lines celebrating God as the creator, Bede preserves them in his 'Ecclesiastical History'. A perfect first Old English text.

lines.english: Now must we praise the Guardian of Heaven,
lines.gloss: Nu = 'now'; sculon = 'must, shall' (modal, 1st plural of sculan); herigean = 'to praise' (infinitive of herian); heofonrices = 'of the heavenly kingdom' (genitive compound); Weard = 'guardian, warden' (accusative singular).

lines.english: the might of the Creator and his mind-thought,
lines.gloss: Meotodes = 'of the Creator' (genitive singular); meahte = 'might, power' (accusative singular); and = 'and'; his = 'his'; modgeþanc = 'mind-thought, intention' (accusative).

lines.original: weorc Wuldor-Fæder, swa he wundra gehwæs,
lines.english: the work of the Father of Glory, as he of every wonder,
lines.gloss: weorc = 'work, deed' (accusative singular); Wuldor-Fæder = 'Father of Glory' (genitive compound); swa = 'as, in the way that'; he = 'he'; wundra = 'of wonders' (genitive plural); gehwæs = 'of each' (genitive of gehwilc).

lines.english: the eternal Lord, established the beginning.
lines.gloss: ece = 'eternal' (nominative); Drihten = 'Lord' (nominative); or = 'beginning, origin' (accusative singular); onstealde = 'established, set up' (past singular of onstellan).

lines.english: He first shaped for the sons of earth
lines.gloss: He = 'he'; ærest = 'first'; sceop = 'shaped, created' (past singular of scieppan); eorðan = 'of the earth' (genitive singular); bearnum = 'for the sons' (dative plural of bearn).

lines.english: heaven as a roof, the holy Creator;
lines.gloss: heofon = 'heaven' (accusative singular); to hrofe = 'as a roof, for a roof' (dative of purpose); halig = 'holy' (nominative); Scyppend = 'Creator' (nominative).

lines.english: then middle-earth, the Guardian of mankind,
lines.gloss: þa = 'then'; middangeard = 'middle-earth, the world' (accusative singular); monncynnes = 'of mankind' (genitive singular compound); Weard = 'Guardian' (nominative).
ece Drihten = 'eternal Lord' (nominative); æfter = 'afterwards'; teode = 'adorned, fashioned' (past singular of teon).

lines.english: the earth for men, the Lord almighty.
lines.gloss: firum = 'for men' (dative plural, poetic); foldan = 'the earth' (accusative singular); Frea = 'Lord' (nominative, poetic); ælmihtig = 'almighty' (nominative).
